subject: Request: Egress fingerprinting & network playbook for SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: SIG Audit Team <sig-audits@verdant-io.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Egress fingerprinting & network playbook for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for taking the time to support Verdant's SIG review. As part of the evidence package we need a concise deliverable that demonstrates how Redwood manages and monitors tenant egress for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A short narrative (1–2 pages) describing the egress "fingerprinting" approach you use to map tenant flows and distinguish customer traffic from platform/controlplane flows.
- A network diagram that highlights control-plane vs data-plane egress boundaries and any NAT/egress gateways used for Private deployments.
- Sample telemetry / pcap or connection logs (redacted) that show the fingerprinting in action (timestamps + flow identifiers).
- A checklist crosswalk tying the above to the relevant CAIQ/SIG questions (network egress, tenant fencing, logging).

Can we get the initial bundle by EOD Monday (2026-11-30)? If that timeline is tight, please propose an alternate. Also include a primary contact for follow-up Q&A.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Senior Security Reviewer
Verdant Security

Hi team,

We've pulled together a compact deliverable that matches Verdant's ask. Outline below and attached artifacts on the shared drive. TL;DR: we can provide the bundle by EOD today.

Deliverables (attached):
- egress_fingerprint_sample.pdf — 2-page narrative describing our fingerprinting heuristics (IP/port clustering, TLS SNI correlation, conntrack tags) and how those are used to mark tenant vs platform flows.
- controlplane_flow_v2.drawio.png — annotated network diagram (control-plane demarcation, egress gateways, mgmt plane NATs).
- tenant-egress-playbook.pdf — excerpt of our Private deployment playbook showing egress gating, approval steps for static egress IP assignment, and operational runbooks for revoking access.
- sig_checklist-completed.xlsx — mapping file to CAIQ questions (network controls, egress, logging).

Notes/Constraints:
- We sanitized telemetry: provided connection summaries and flow hashes instead of raw PCAPs. Legal approved the sanitized samples; full PCAPs require explicit customer consent.
- For Dedicated (shared hardware pools with tenant tagging), we show how KV-cache isolation + VPC egress translation are logged and correlated. For Private (VPC-on-prem), the playbook documents the customer-managed egress gate and our recommended hardening posture.
- Primary contact for follow-up: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai (I'll join the Q&A).

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm the redaction steps on the telemetry files and upload the sanitized CSV by noon.
- Dylan: add the exact runbook section numbers to the playbook PDF (so Verdant can reference).

I'll upload everything to the link below and send Verdant the bundle + short intro.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Uploaded sanitized telemetry and checklist to the drive link. Summary of what I included:

- telemetry_sample_sanitized.csv — connection summaries with flow_hash (sha256 of conn tuple + timestamp), bytes, duration, labelled tenant_id where available. No customer payloads or IP addresses that would identify internal endpoints.
- redaction_report.txt — lines documenting the redaction pattern applied (IP->range, hostname->sni-hash). Legal sign-off included.

I also added a short appendix to the playbook (page 4) listing the logs we keep for egress investigation and retention windows (30/90/365 days depending on log type).

Let me know if Verdant requests raw PCAPs — per policy we need explicit consent from the customer and a signed NDA.

Kimberly Park
Manager, Security Architectures | Redwood Inference
